args.body:
Hi Dora! I just had a look at your personal website (www.dora-website.com) and wanted to share some feedback.

What I liked:
- It's clean and easy to load — no clutter, no pop-ups, no autoplay media. The page reads instantly.
- The contact e-mail is right there on the page, so it's easy for visitors to reach you.

What could be improved:
- The site is very bare right now — it's essentially one line of text. There's nothing that tells visitors who you are, what you do, or what you're interested in.
- Consider adding a short intro/bio, a few sections (e.g. work, projects, writing, hobbies), and links to your other profiles or projects.
- A bit of visual design would help it feel like a real personal site — even a simple layout with headings, images, and a consistent color scheme goes a long way.
- You might also add a small "About" or "Contact" page, and consider a contact form so people don't have to expose your e-mail publicly.

Overall it's a nice, clean starting point — it just needs a little more content and personality to really shine. Nice work getting it live!

Best,
Emma Johnson

Hi Eve! I just had a look at your blog (www.eve-blog.com) and wanted to share some feedback.

What I liked:
- The site is clean and loads quickly, with a simple, no-friction reading experience.
- The personal touch about hiking is a nice hook — it gives visitors an idea of who you are and what you write about.

What could be improved:
- The blog doesn't have any actual posts yet, so there's nothing for readers to dig into. Publishing a few entries (even short ones) would give the site a reason to exist.
- Since hiking is your favorite hobby, that would make a great theme for a series — trail guides, gear notes, trip recaps, or photo essays.
- Add an archive and/or categories/tags so returning readers can find older posts easily.
- An "About" page, a subscribe option (RSS or newsletter), and links to your social profiles would help build an audience.
- A little visual polish — a header image, consistent typography, and mobile-friendly layouts — would make it feel more like a real blog.

Overall it's a nice, tidy foundation. With a few posts and some structure, it could become a really enjoyable place to share your hiking stories.

Best,
Emma Johnson
